Reason: The image displays a well-circumscribed, ovoid mass in the anterior mediastinum with a prominent, thick calcified rim (often described as an "eggshell" calcification), which is a characteristic radiographic feature of a mature teratoma. While fat-fluid levels are also specific to teratomas, they are not clearly visualized in this particular slice, making the calcified margin the most consistent finding among the choices.
